;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Hanau shootings]]
**Nine people are killed and five others injured in two [[mass shooting]]s at [[Hookah lounge|shisha bars]] in [[Hanau]], [[Hesse]], [[Germany]]. The attacker also [[matricide|kills his mother]] [[murder-suicide|and]] [[suicide|then himself]] in their apartment. He expressed [[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|far-right]] views in a letter of confession and video. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/19/shooting-germany-hanau-dead-several-people-shisha-near-frankfurt (''The Guardian'')]
**Twelve [[Somali soldier]]s are killed when a [[suicide attack|suicide bomber]] and gunmen storm a [[military base]] in [[Lower Shabelle]]. The militants briefly capture the base before it is reclaimed. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claim responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-attacks/somali-militants-kill-12-soldiers-in-attack-on-base-say-officials-idUSKBN20D1MJ (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] calls a Turkish intervention in [[Syria]]'s [[Idlib Governorate]] "imminent" after talks with [[Russia]] fail to reach what he describes as their "desired result". Erdoğan threatens to launch an operation in Idlib by the end of the month. [[Kremlin]] Press Secretary [[Dmitry Peskov]] calls [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish]] involvement in the battle "the worst scenario". The countries support opposing sides in the war. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/president-erdogan-threatens-imminent-turkish-operation-syria-200219092248649.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[Ceasefire]] talks between the [[House of Representatives (Libya)|Tobruk-led government]] and the [[Government of National Accord|GNA]] are suspended as rocket attacks bombard [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-51557970 (BBC News)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)]]
**A convoy carrying [[Yemen]]i Defense Minister [[Mohammed Ali Al-Maqdashi]] in [[Ma'rib Governorate]] strikes a [[landmine]], killing six people. The Defense Minister survives the blast. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/yemeni-defense-minister-survives-explosion-6-killed/1738681 (Anadolu Agency)]

;Business and economy
*The assets of American [[fast fashion]] chain [[Forever 21]] are purchased out of bankruptcy by [[real estate]] companies [[Simon Property Group]] and [[Brookfield Property Partners]], and [[brand management]] firm [[Authentic Brands Group]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-forever21-bankruptcy/forever-21-snapped-up-by-mall-owners-authentic-brands-idUSKBN20D2MH (Reuters)]
*The American [[S&P 500]] and [[NASDAQ Composite]] stock-market indexes hit all-time closing highs. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/02/19/stock-market-wall-street-in-focus-amid-coronavirus-outbreak.html (CNBC)] 

;Disasters and accidents
*Aftermath of the [[Malaysia Airlines Flight 370]]
**Former [[Australian Prime Minister]] [[Tony Abbott]] says that high-ranking Malaysian officials believed pilot Zaharie Ahmad Shah deliberately downed the plane. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/malaysia-airlines-flight-370-pilot-suspected-mass-suicide-government-australiam-pm-plane (Fox News)]
;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
***[[Iran]] reports its first two cases of the virus. Hours later, it was announced both infected people have died. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/iran-reports-its-first-2-cases-of-the-new-coronavirus/ (''Times of Israel'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/die-coronavirus-iran-fatalities-middle-east-200219171007605.html (Al Jazerra)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
***The [[Tokyo Marathon]] reduces the number of runners from 38,000 to an elite group of 200 due to the rising coronavirus fear. [http://www.newsonjapan.com/html/newsdesk/article/126400.php (NOJ)]
***Hundreds of passengers aboard the ''[[Diamond Princess (ship)|Diamond Princess]]'' are allowed to disembark the ship. The vessel has been [[quarantine]]d since docking in [[Yokohama]] on 4 February. Criticism mounts against the [[Government of Japan|Japanese government]]'s handling of the quarantine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-idUSKBN20D02U (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*Murder of [[Bashar Barakah Jackson]]
**Bashar Barakah Jackson, also known as ‘[[Pop Smoke]]’, is killed in [[Los Angeles]], [[United States]]. The cause of death was multiple gunshot wounds to his torso, inflicted by a teenager during a targeted home invasion that went wrong. Pop Smoke was a rising rapper from [[Brooklyn]], and had just released his second mixtape ‘[[Meet the Woo 2]]’. He rented an [[apartment]] in the [[Hollywood Hills]] a few days prior to his murder for a simple vacation. The day before his [[homicide]], he accidentally leaked his address online via social media, giving the location to it’s murderers, which tragically ended his life the age of 20 years old.
[https://www.complex.com/music/2020/02/pop-smoke-killed-during-home-invasion-robbery (Pop Smoke Shot Dead)]
*[[Murder of Hannah Clarke]]
**A mother and her three children are killed in a car fire in [[Brisbane]], [[Australia]], in a targeted [[familicide]] [[carjacking]] by former [[New Zealand Warriors]] player Rowan Baxter. He was the ex-husband of the woman and father of the children, and he committed [[suicide]] at the scene. [https://www.news.com.au/national/queensland/hannah-baxter-dies-after-burns-in-horrific-fire-incident/news-story/276ceb3a836aad23a1984c7438e00d1d (News.com.au)]
*[[China]] expels three journalists of ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' over an opinion piece called "China Is the Real Sick Man of Asia" that was deemed [[racist]]. The [[government of China|government]] demanded the newspaper apologize, which it declined. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman [[Geng Shuang]] says the journalists have five days to leave the country and says the article "denigrated" China's efforts to combat the virus. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-51558310 (BBC News)]
*[[Senate of Brazil|Brazilian Senator]] [[Cid Gomes]] is shot during a clash with striking [[Military Police (Brazil)|military police officers]] in [[Sobral, Ceará]].  [https://news.yahoo.com/brazilian-senator-shot-amid-tumult-221345361.html (AP via Yahoo News)]
*[[Corruption in Mexico]], [[Operation Car Wash]]
**[[Law enforcement in Mexico|Mexican law enforcement]] launches a corruption inquiry into former [[President of Mexico|President]] [[Enrique Peña Nieto]], as part of a larger investigation into bribery and [[money laundering]] by former [[Pemex]] CEO [[Emilio Lozoya Austin]] involving [[Brazil]]ian conglomerate [[Odebrecht]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-corruption/former-mexico-president-pena-nieto-investigated-in-corruption-probe-report-idUSKBN20E01N?il=0 (Reuters)] 

;Politics and elections
*The [[Dominican Republic]] government fires 139 [[Foreign minister|Foreign Ministry officials]]. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/02/19/dominican-gov-purges-the-foreign-service-fires-139-officials/ (''Dominican Today'')]
*The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Home Secretary]] [[Priti Patel]] announces a reform of the UK's immigration system. The changes includes the end of [[freedom of movement]], a minimum requirement of migrants to speak [[English language|English]], a minimum salary of between [[pound sterling|£]]20,480 and £25,600, while priority will be given to skilled workers over non-skilled migrants. The changes are effective from January 1, 2021. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-51550421 (BBC News)]
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**A recanvass of the [[2020 Iowa Democratic caucuses]] show [[Bernie Sanders]] and [[Pete Buttigieg]] at an effective tie, with a margin of 0.0004 percentage points of state delegate equivalents between the two candidates. The Sanders campaign has requested a recount, which may change the initial outcome of the caucus. [https://apnews.com/74508879cd193d3ba1f3b75909c0945e (AP)]
